title: m.iMX RT:  After a few seconds print() hangs
body:
Attempting to run [simple_benchmarks.py ](https://github.com/kevinjwalters/circuitpython-examples/blob/master/benchmarks/simple_benchmarks.py) crashed (hung) MP on my Teensy 4.1 .
 I reduced the program maximally to:
```
import time

def timeit(func, arg):
    t1 = time.ticks_us()
    func(arg)
    t2 = time.ticks_us()
    return time.ticks_diff(t2, t1) / 1e6

def bm_001AdditionA(n):
    for idx in range(n):
        if idx % 50 == 0:
            a = 1.0
            b = 1.1
            c = 3.456789e-4
            d = 5.678901e4
            f = 1.5
        a += 1.01
        b = a + b
        c = c + a + a + a
        d = a + b + 0.9999
        e = a + b + c + d
    return (a, b, c, d, e)

print('Start..', end='')
for _ in range(5):
    timeit(bm_001AdditionA, 50000)
    time.sleep(0.1)                                            # including this leads to a hang
    # print('.', end="")                                       # but including this runs through
print('Finish')
```
and still it hangs.
Strangely including the `print('.', end="")` leads to ordinary run through.
Commenting that statement out still runs through, but as soon as `time.sleep(0.1)` is uncommented it hangs again.
A combination of timing and printing leading to a crash..

For reproducing I installed the latest MP:
MicroPython v1.19.1-782-g699477d12 on 2022-12-20; Teensy 4.1 with MIMXRT1062DVJ6A.

> With the teensy after os.dupterm(uart) the serial line mirrored all in- and outputs on USB (i.e. /dev/ttyACM0) but not the other way round: What was communicated on serial did not appear on USB.

In my set-up using dupterm with REPL everything that is received or sent appears on both channels. That's the way it's implemented. See mphalport.c, function mp_hal_stdout_tx_strn(). There is a check for tud_cdc_connected() before writing to USB. So if the connection was lost, only write to UART happens. 

The RP2040 and SAMD use TinyUSB as well and are implemented almost identical.
Edit: There is no relation between TinyUSB and the MIMXRT serial. They use completely different libraries.

Tested with both a Teensy 4.1 and a RT1052 Dev Board.

P.S.: With the changed test5a script, there are indeed no memory or assert failures, since it does not allocate more RAM. The problem occurred after the sequence:
1. frequent allocation of RAM for growing strings, but not until automatic garbage collection runs.
2. frequent allocation of RAM for floats, such that automatic garbage collections start.
3. then it crashes during one the next attempts to allocate RAM.

2. does not happen with the new test5a().

Do you know what MICROPY_EVENT_POLL_HOOK and __WFE() do?
The difference between the RP2040 and MiMXRT versions of mp_hal_stdout_tx_strn is that RP2040 executes
MICROPY_EVENT_POLL_HOOK `while (n > tud_cdc_write_available())` and the  MiMXRT  __WFE() .

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
It may be a USB connection issue. Which PC OS do you run? Is the device directly connected to the PC or though a USB hub. Is a modem manager active on the PC?

> Do you know what MICROPY_EVENT_POLL_HOOK and __WFE() do?

MICROPY_EVENT_POLL_HOOK is a macro defined in mpconfigport.h. It is usually called in wait loops and checks for tasks to be scheduled. One of the instructions in MICROPY_EVENT_POLL_HOOK is usually either the __WFE() or __WFI() instruction. Both are ARM instructions and set the CPU to low power mode until an event or interrupt happens, which is at least the timer tick interrupt every 1 ms. You can drop __WFE() for test, if you like. But that should not make a difference, because is the code hangs there, the serial print will either be delayed or not happen.

For the memory issue I'll open a separate issue item.
